conf.description: Oracle Database Audit, listener, xml-file (ADR log.xml): extracts the <msg> envelope (time, host_id, host_addr, pid, comp_id, org_id, type, level) then reuses the listener/other two-stage TNS walk on the <txt> body - per recommendations.direct.cribl, this is that pipeline's XML branch, not a new parser.

conf.comment: listener / xml-file. Assumes the Source already delivers one <msg>...</msg> record as one event's _raw - splitting the ADR log.xml stream on that boundary is a Source-level Event Breaker Ruleset concern, out of scope for this pipeline (Sources are not touched here). msg attribute order is not assumed - each is matched with an independent lookahead. Envelope 'time' is authoritative and used for _time; the <txt> body's own leading DD-MON-YYYY timestamp is intentionally not extracted here. Numeric ADR 'level' has no documented level-to-ECS-log.level table in the work order, so it is left as a raw duplicate field rather than guessed (gap, see README) - same treatment as an unremovable numeric path segment. Body field mappings (service.name, source.ip, event.action, error.code/event.outcome, etc.) are identical to the listener/other pipeline and share its same scope/gaps (establish-shape lines only, unverified regex against a real sample).

functions.description: extract the <msg> envelope attributes (order-independent, via lookaheads) and the <txt> body text in one pass
same CONNECT_DATA sub-group walk as listener/other, run once connect_inner is pulled out of the <txt> body below

pull the CONNECT_DATA/ADDRESS blobs, event, trailing SID|Service segment (unmapped, not in this work order's field list) and return code out of the <txt> body - the body's own leading timestamp is skipped since the msg time attribute is authoritative
walk the ADDRESS sub-group extracted from the <txt> body
batch rename the envelope and body straight-copy captures; CID HOST stays a custom claim field, never overwriting the observer-verified source.ip

_time from the authoritative msg time attribute (ISO 8601 with offset, no timezone reconstruction needed), process.pid/source.port/error.code cast to number, tcps flagged as TLS-wrapped TNS, event.outcome derived from the return code, event.dataset tagged for the shared logs-oracle.listener stream; 'level' (raw numeric ADR severity) is deliberately left in the event unmapped - no level-to-log.level table was supplied, so it is kept as a harmless duplicate rather than guessed
Re-nest flat dotted keys (data-maps canonical step)
